taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce angusta is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: FIRST CHECK THE LEAVES: E. angusta (narrowleaf spurge) is an ERECT, narrow-leaved perennial, not a creeping sandmat. Upper leaves are extremely narrow—typically more than six times longer than wide. Look for short white appressed (strigose) hairs on leaves and stems, small reddish-brown stipule projections at nodes, and green hairy cyathial cups edged by toothed white gland appendages. FNA describes HAIRY CAPSULES and pale 4-angled lightly wrinkled mature seeds, but the currently licensed macro set proves hairy cyathial cups NOT independently a mature hairy capsule or a loose seed. Contrast with low rounded-leaved glabrous E. fendleri. Formal BONAP/NAPA county nativity decision stays on HOLD.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew accepts Euphorbia angusta, native from western Texas to Coahuila.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. In E. angusta, the combination of erect perennial habit, very narrow distal leaves, uniform strigose pubescence, and hairy fruit is unusually distinctive.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Perennial with moderately to strongly thickened rootstock; stems erect, about 12–43 cm.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite. Proximal blades ovate to ovate-elliptic; distal blades linear to elliptic-linear, about 7–41 × 2–5 mm and more than 6× as long as wide. Base asymmetric, cuneate to rounded; margins entire; apex acute; surfaces usually short-strigose.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, linear-subulate or reduced to nodiform/papilliform structures, often reddish brown, about 0.1–0.7 mm, strigose.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Solitary at distal nodes. Involucre strigose; 4 narrow oblong green to yellow-green glands with relatively showy white flabellate appendages whose distal margins are shallowly and irregularly toothed.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 2–2.6 × 2.5–3 mm, strigose.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds white, ovoid, 4-angled in cross section, about 1.7–2.2 × 1.1–1.2 mm, transversely low-ridged or wrinkled.
best_field_traits: distal leaves linear to elliptic-linear and more than 6× as long as wide
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. fendleri, E. angusta is much taller and erect, with very narrow distal leaves and a hairy capsule; E. fendleri is a low clustered perennial with rounded entire glabrous leaves and glabrous capsule. Against the prostrate sandmats, the erect narrow-leaved silhouette is the quickest first split.

learner_visual_status.note: Crew can identify narrow-leaf growth, appressed pubescence, stipule locations and toothed white cyathial appendages. Exact capsule hairs, mature seed and publicly reusable whole-rooted habit remain photography gaps. Two UT photos withheld.

comparisons.key_distinctions: The easiest field package is erect + narrow distal leaves + uniform short strigose hairs. The hairy capsule then confirms it against low glabrous-fruited perennial E. fendleri.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: START WITH LONG NARROW LEAVES; THEN CHECK HAIRS AND FLOWER CUPS
steps: Find an erect leafy plant; photograph its full branching habit and the position of the narrowest upper leaves (FNA: distal blades often >6× as long as wide).
At the node take paired upper leaves in focus, then look for short closely appressed white hairs with a macro view.
Under 10× look for two tiny reddish-brown stipule projections by leaf bases; they are distinct from ordinary pale hairs.
Find a tiny solitary cyathium at a branch tip: observe the GREEN HAIRY INVOLUCRE (cup) and toothed white gland appendages; these are not ordinary petals.
For a FULL identification, photograph a separate mature three-lobed fruit so capsule hairs can be identified independently of involucre hairs.
Optional final seed check: true detached white, 4-angled seed with low transverse wrinkles next to a millimeter ruler. Do not mistake capsule for seed.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Becky Brenner and Nathan Taylor cyathial views support involucre pubescence, not independent capsule hairs. No photographed mature white seed is currently present. Two UT images still have no verified public redistribution rights. Nathan's 08/09 photos are single-expert identified and carry a provisional identity warning.
